added.claim: JsonBodyReader.isJsonType returns false (so req.body gives 415) for a JSON media type whose charset parameter is anything other than utf-8 (e.g. application/json; charset=iso-8859-1). The 415 itself matches Express body-parser, but docs/api/request.md only says 415 happens when the Content-Type is not JSON, and never mentions that only UTF-8 is accepted. A client sending a declared non-UTF-8 charset gets a 415 the docs do not explain.
added.suggested_fix: In docs/api/request.md's JSON section, say that the body is read as UTF-8 only, that a charset parameter other than utf-8 gives 415 (as in Express body-parser), and spell out which +json types are accepted (application/<x>+json).

added.claim: A JSON body that starts with a UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF) is rejected with 400. The reader skips only space, tab, CR and LF before handing off to the strict Gson reader, which then sees U+FEFF. Express body-parser decodes through iconv-lite, which strips the BOM, so it accepts these bodies. Neither the spec nor docs/api settles this, so it is an undocumented Express-compat gap rather than a contract breach.
added.evidence: NaruServe-api/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/internal/JsonBodyReader.java (whitespace skip loop before codec.decode); no BOM rule in docs/spec or docs/api (grep BOM/FEFF: none)
added.suggested_fix: Either skip one leading U+FEFF in the pre-read loop (one condition, with a test), or state in docs/api/request.md that a BOM-prefixed body gets 400.
